oewn-07321790-n.learner: a set of connected events that together make up one episode
examples: The holiday turned into a chapter of accidents, one after another.

oewn-08245759-n.learner: a church meeting of the monks of a monastery, or even of the canons of a church
examples: The abbot called the monks together for a chapter.

oewn-03665990-n.learner: a place built to hold books and other materials so that people can read and study them
examples: The old papers were moved to a library built for scholars to study them.

oewn-07994015-n.learner: in computing, a set of standard programs and small routines that are stored and ready to use at once
examples: The program calls a maths library to do its sums.

oewn-08585785-n.learner: the surroundings and situation in which something is set
examples: Change of scene might be of service

oewn-07022924-n.learner: one of the parts that an act of a play or show is divided into
examples: The ghost appears in the second scene of the first act.

oewn-14429707-n.learner: a time when someone shows their bad temper
examples: She made a scene when the waiter brought the wrong dish.

connotation.why: frames an outburst as an embarrassing display rather than plain anger

oewn-13960108-n.learner: a situation thought of as a whole thing that you can look at and describe
examples: The music scene in the city has changed a lot in ten years.

oewn-06627082-n.learner: a run of pictures in a film, one after another, that together show one piece of action
examples: The chase scene took three days to film.

oewn-04152121-n.learner: the painted pieces of a stage set that are meant to make it look like a certain place
examples: While the curtain was down, the workers shifted the scenes and rolled in a painted forest.

oewn-04151847-n.learner: a drawn or photographed picture of something as it looks to the eye
examples: She painted a winter scene of skaters on a frozen pond.
Her face showed the trouble she felt about her son.

oewn-07387165-n.learner: a disturbance in which people are angry
examples: There was trouble outside the ground after the match.

oewn-14070233-n.learner: a pregnancy that was not wanted
examples: He got her in trouble and then left town.

connotation.why: names a pregnancy as a misfortune or disgrace

oewn-00019441-v.learner: to act on something in a physical way; to have an effect on it
examples: The disease mainly affects the lungs.

oewn-02682907-v.learner: to link someone closely with something, often in a way that suggests they are guilty
examples: Papers found in the office affected two officials in the fraud.

connotation.why: often implies guilt in the person it links

oewn-13881240-n.learner: a difference between two states, especially between how things were before and after something happened
examples: Friends noticed the change in him after the accident.

oewn-11432841-n.learner: what you have after something has been altered or modified
examples: The tailor's changes made the coat fit perfectly.

oewn-13409284-n.learner: coins of small value, thought of all together
examples: He had a pocket full of change for the bus.

oewn-13408862-n.learner: the money you get back when you pay more than the amount you owe
examples: She handed over a ten and waited for her change.

oewn-13408652-n.learner: money you get in return for the same amount in a larger note or coin, or in a different currency
examples: Can you give me change for a twenty?
The only change on the menu was a new soup.

oewn-03009373-n.learner: a different or fresh set of clothes
examples: Pack a change of clothes in case you get wet.
We remember the dead and care for the living.

oewn-11523478-n.learner: the way a moving wave of light or sound is thrown back when it meets a surface
examples: An echo is caused by the reflection of sound from the cliffs.

oewn-06893299-n.learner: a way that something is shown without words
examples: Her tired face was a reflection of the long night she had had.

oewn-04754355-n.learner: a copy or likeness of something in which left and right are swapped
examples: The letter b is a reflection of the letter d.

oewn-05017811-n.learner: the ability of something to throw back beams or rays
examples: The high reflection of snow makes it painfully bright in sunlight.

oewn-13807616-n.learner: in mathematics, a transformation in which the direction of one axis is turned the other way
examples: A reflection in the y-axis turns the point (2, 3) into (-2, 3).

oewn-06208877-n.learner: a willingness to support someone, to stay loyal to them, or to agree with an opinion.
examples: I knew I could count on her understanding when I told her what I had done.

oewn-00051593-s.learner: having the qualities needed for something
examples: The new manager proved capable of the task.

oewn-02370095-s.learner: that could possibly accept or allow something
examples: The rule is capable of more than one reading.
